podcast.title: Soviet State-Commissioned Rock Band (1968)
podcast.body: In 1968, the Soviet state commissioned the creation of an official rock band called "The Happy Guys." This clean-cut group was tasked with singing songs promoting a positive view of the world and emphasizing the greatness of the USSR. However, this attempt to create state-approved rock music was ultimately unsuccessful in achieving its propaganda goals. "In 1968, the state commissioned the creation of an official rock band. Yeah, a Soviet rock band created by the Soviet state."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Great KGB Punk Rock Conspiracy

podcast.title: State-Commissioned Soviet Rock Band
podcast.body: In 1968, the Soviet state commissioned the creation of an "official rock band" known as The Happy Guys. This clean-cut group was tasked with singing songs that affirmed the positivity of the world and specifically lauded the greatness of the USSR, an attempt by the authorities to control the narrative of rock music. "They were a clean cut bunch called the Happy Guys, and they sang songs that said the world is fine, and the USSR is especially great."
